summary: Ephemeral cross-account access for CostOps: AWS AssumeRole + GCP Workload Identity to read billing & audit logs
description:
Issue summary: CostOps needs temporary, auditable, least-privilege read access to billing exports and Cloud Audit Logs across a subset of prod and staging projects in both AWS and GCP. Request is for an ephemeral access flow (max 8 hours) using AWS AssumeRole with short-lived credentials and GCP Workload Identity Federation for human-triggered sessions via the existing access portal.

Background: The Finance/CostOps team needs to investigate a billing anomaly impacting several teams in us-east1 and eu-west1. Historically we provisioned long-lived IAM roles which create blast radius and auditing gaps. Security policy favors ephemeral, just-in-time access, scoped to read-only resources and logged with session-level metadata.

Request: 1) Create an AWS IAM role (arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/CostOpsBillingReadOnly-Ephemeral) with a trust policy allowing sts:AssumeRole only from our SSO/OIDC broker and session tags for requestor. Attach a policy limiting actions to s3:GetObject on billing buckets (redwood-prod-billing-*, redwood-staging-billing-*) and logs:DescribeLogGroups and logs:GetLogEvents on specific log groups.
2) Configure GCP Workload Identity binding to allow ephemeral human identities issued by our identity broker to impersonate a service account (projects/redwood-prod/serviceAccounts/costops-ephemeral@redwood-prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com) with roles/logging.viewer and roles/storage.objectViewer limited to billing buckets.
3) Enforce max session duration = 8h, require MFA at time of issuance, and emit a session_cert with requestor username, request_id, and justification.
4) Add audit dashboards to the Console's internal view and a pre-built query for CostOps to show actions performed during the session.

Impact: This will enable CostOps to access necessary data to complete the billing investigation without creating persistent privileged accounts. Risk is low if policies are scoped properly; primary risk vectors are overbroad resource ARNs or missing session tagging.

Environment: prod and staging projects in GCP (redwood-prod, redwood-staging) and AWS account 123456789012 (prod) and 210987654321 (staging). Regions: us-east1, eu-west1.

Steps already attempted: - CostOps attempted cross-account role assume via existing portal but got AccessDenied when trying to list billing buckets. Error below. - Verified that the portal is issuing tokens; failure appears due to missing trust policy and missing storage permissions.

Error snippet: "AccessDenied: User: arn:aws:sts::123456789012:assumed-role/PortalSession/priya.n needs permission s3:ListBucket for resource redwood-prod-billing-2026"

Proposed minimal AWS policy (example):
{
  "Version": "2012-10-17",
  "Statement": [
    {"Effect": "Allow","Action": ["s3:GetObject", "s3:ListBucket"],"Resource": ["arn:aws:s3:::redwood-prod-billing-*", "arn:aws:s3:::redwood-staging-billing-*/*"]},
    {"Effect": "Allow","Action": ["logs:DescribeLogGroups", "logs:GetLogEvents"],"Resource": ["arn:aws:logs:us-east-1:123456789012:log-group:/billing/*"]}
  ]
}

Proposed minimal GCP IAM binding (example):
- Service Account: costops-ephemeral@redwood-prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com
- Roles: roles/storage.objectViewer (limited to projects/redwood-prod/buckets/redwood-prod-billing-*), roles/logging.viewer (limited to the billing log sinks)

Approval & audit: Requesting Security approval from @Elena Park for the proposed trust policies and session tagging scheme. Once approved, infra should implement role creation + portal wiring, then Security and CostOps will test in staging before prod roll-out.

Follow-ups: - Add automation to auto-revoke any sessions older than 8h. - Add a monthly review to ensure ARNs remain scoped correctly.
